_note: Admission test: a delegated result is inherited as finished work by default. If nobody inspects it, later work is built on an unverified artifact and the missing observation cannot be reconstructed after the session ends; healing requires discarding the inherited result and restarting the work, path (3). The verdict row warns that a broad Read/Glob/Grep discharge can license one unit with activity about another. Tool-name events expose no shared unit or artifact operand, so an extractor would abstain rather than protect; this clause tightens the observable guard to an actual Read and activates only after dispatch. The remaining session-level approximation is admitted only if the frozen-corpus measurement reports no candidate false positives and its terminal firing rate stays below HIGH_INTERRUPT.

waiver.because: NOT EVALUABLE against this host: no exit status reaches PostToolUse in any form. Measured over 71 recorded Bash PostToolUse payloads in makoto.record.db (the raw hook events, not the transcript): tool_response is a dict in every one, keyed (stdout, stderr, interrupted, isImage, noOutputExpected), plus returnCodeInterpretation once carrying the string 'No matches found'. No exit_code member under any spelling, and no 'Error: Exit code N' string -- that form is the TRANSCRIPT's rendering of a failed call, not the payload. Failing runs do produce PostToolUse events, so the clause is not merely unobserved: the evidence it asks for is absent from an event that arrives. Matching failure text in tool_response.stdout was measured instead and rejected: it fired on a real failure AND on a passing run (121 passed, 1 xfailed) in an 18-run sample, and predicates over prose are what this table exists to avoid. Ledger cost of leaving it live: 114 demand rows in one session, 0 discharges ever, every Stop blocked. Renew only by re-arguing this research; if the host ships an exit status, delete the waiver instead.

_fixture_note: terminal keyed clause: fixtures_pos/neg validate the PostToolUse failure guard; fixtures_activate validate checker recognition. The guard reads tool_response as TEXT, not tool_response.exit_code: the host sends no exit-code field. A SUCCEEDING Bash call yields a dict keyed (stdout, stderr, interrupted, isImage, noOutputExpected); a FAILING one yields the STRING 'Error: Exit code N\n<output>'. Measured over 2279 recorded tool results (1985 dict / 175 str / 119 list, 67 distinct keys) -- no exit_code member under any spelling. The engine returns False for a non-str under kind=regex, so the success dict cannot discharge and only a real failure does.
_note: Individual admission decision: a checker that accepts missing or invalid input produces the same green result as a sound checker, so doing nothing preserves a false licensing fact and downstream work consumes the opportunity to distinguish them. Recovery requires reversing the accepted PASS, planting or removing input, and replaying the checker decision path (restart path 3). The occasion is narrowed to explicit pytest/unittest runners and named *check*/verify Python or shell scripts. Each PreToolUse activation records the normalized checker command as its own obligation; only a nonzero PostToolUse for the equal key discharges it. Admit only if the frozen corpus reports candidate_fp=0 and TABLE_SUM remains below 20 per 1000. 2026-08-20: the command-word class excludes = and quote characters. It was [^\s;&|]*, which a shell VARIABLE ASSIGNMENT satisfies -- F=plugin/makoto/checks/writeThrashRevert.py contains 'check' and ends .py, so it both activated the clause and became the key, and nothing can discharge a row that names no runnable checker. A genuine invocation never carries = inside the program token, and 'export PYTHONPATH=/x; python3 -m pytest tests/' still keys off its second segment. See tests/test_c08_activation.py.

occasion: the trace is about to infer process presence from a ps pipeline whose checker can appear in its own result
costly: count or trust a grep-shaped process match without excluding the observer identity

subject: session_id

_note: Admission test: a checker included in its own observation can create a stable false-positive process count. That apparent presence is then used as fact, and repeated checks reproduce the same observer contamination; doing nothing never reveals the absent target. Recovery requires interrupting the accepted result and rerunning from a correctly separated observer, effectively restarting the decision path (3). The verdict's broad pgrep/pkill/killall branch is narrowed away because it does not require a grep process in a ps pipeline and would interrupt ordinary process operations unrelated to self-inclusion. The remaining fingerprint names the concrete self-match surface, while the guard requires an identity-bearing inverted filter rather than a name-only grep trick.

occasion: the trace is about to present a plan for adoption
costly: adopt a plan built on nothing read
guard: read something first, so the plan describes this repository and not a remembered one
subject: session_id
deny_reason: present a plan with no read, glob or grep on record; a plan is followed by default, so a plan built on assumption defines the whole path before anything is checked
_note: Measured hole: 29 ExitPlanMode calls in one session, zero clauses. A plan is the perfect asymmetry -- it defines the path and its end, and nobody decides to follow it.

occasion: the trace is about to present a plan whose ambiguities were settled by guessing
costly: adopt a plan built on a guessed reading of the request
guard: ask one question about the ambiguity before the plan is fixed
subject: session_id
deny_reason: present a plan with no question asked this session; reading files resolves what the repository is, never what was wanted, and a plan is followed by default
_note: P01 guards the same occasion and accepts Read/Glob/Grep as discharge, which answers a different question: reading establishes what the repository IS, not what was ASKED FOR. A plan can therefore be adopted having read forty files and asked nothing, and P01 counts it discharged. The two failure modes are independent -- a plan grounded in the tree can still be a plan for the wrong task -- so this is a separate clause rather than a widened P01. Against the admission test: left alone, a plan built on a guessed reading is FOLLOWED, because a plan's default is adoption and nothing in the run re-opens the interpretation. The state it leaves is work completed under the wrong goal, and that heals only by throwing the session away and starting over -- path (3), an ACTION, and the most expensive one. Its interruption cost is bounded by the occasion: ExitPlanMode is rare per session and one question discharges it for the whole session.

occasion: the trace is about to switch or check out a git ref
costly: switch or check out a git ref
guard: know the ref exists: `git rev-parse --verify REF`, or have created it yourself with `git checkout -b/-B REF` or `git branch REF`
deny_reason: switch or check out a git ref that was never verified or created this session; run `git rev-parse --verify REF`, or create it with `git checkout -b/-B REF`
_natural_guard: Creating a ref is discharged by work someone actually does: `git checkout -B REF origin/main` is how a session makes the branch it later returns to, and creation is the strongest possible proof the ref exists. Measured on the frozen corpus: the sole U09 denial checked out `claude/gyroscope-terminal-clauses`, a branch the same session had created 12 calls earlier with `git checkout -B` -- the guard was already run, under a name the old discharged_by refused to see. `git rev-parse --verify` remains the explicit probe for refs the session did not make.

guard: look at the structure first: `jq 'keys'`, `jq 'type'`, `jq -e 'has(...)'`, or any jq structure assertion on the same file
deny_reason: traverse structured JSON whose structure was never once looked at; run `jq 'keys'`, `jq 'type'`, or a `jq -e` type/key assertion on the file first
_natural_guard: The old guard demanded specifically `jq -e` with a type/has assertion -- a ritual observed 0 times in 2152 real Bash calls. The observation people actually make before traversing a JSON file is `jq 'keys'` or `jq 'type'` on it: measured on the frozen corpus, the session ran `jq 'keys' FILE` before every per-file traversal chain (e.g. call 2100 `jq 'keys' calibration_preregistered.json` precedes 2104 `jq 'del(.tasks)'` on the same file). That look is the guard -- it answers the same question (what shape is this document) and is discharged by work that is already part of the job. `jq -e` still discharges.
